answer: Each identity claims one reef ledge, locks an 80-credit bond, plants a juniper stake at its start, and mounts a prism reflector at the end. It files the angle and stake distance; an auditor re-measures both against the angle table and burns the bond on a mismatch over 2 percent or a missing juniper stake. First costs 41, the kth costs 41+3(k-1), the 1,000th costs 3,038, 1,000 fakes cost 1,539,500 plus 80,000 locked, each reef ledge needing its own stake, reflector, and survey. A rented-prism ring fails on one serial on two ledges; an honest agent pays 41 once and recovers it after audit.
